name: Energy Chemistry
tagline: Hydrogen economy, solar fuels, and next-generation energy storage.
seo_title: Energy Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Energy Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in batteries, hydrogen, solar materials, biofuels and carbon capture.

definition.lead: Energy chemistry studies how energy is stored, converted and released in chemical form: fuels, batteries, hydrogen and solar materials.
definition.body: Moving from fossil fuels to low-carbon energy is, above all, a chemistry problem. Better battery electrodes, cheaper hydrogen catalysts, efficient solar absorbers and carbon capture all start in the chemistry lab.

timeline.title: The battery
timeline.text: Alessandro Volta builds the voltaic pile.

timeline.title: The photovoltaic effect
timeline.text: Edmond Becquerel observes a current when light shines on an electrode.
timeline.why: The physics behind every solar cell.

timeline.title: The oil age
timeline.text: Edwin Drake drills a commercial oil well in Pennsylvania.
timeline.why: Petroleum began to reshape energy and chemistry.

timeline.title: Nuclear chain reaction
timeline.text: Chicago Pile-1 achieves the first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction.

timeline.title: The silicon solar cell
timeline.text: Bell Labs demonstrates a practical silicon solar cell.

timeline.title: A better cathode
timeline.text: John Goodenough's team identifies lithium cobalt oxide as a cathode.
timeline.why: Gave lithium-ion batteries their high voltage.

timeline.title: Perovskite solar cells
timeline.text: Akihiro Kojima, Tsutomu Miyasaka and colleagues report perovskite solar cells.
timeline.why: Efficiencies rose faster than for any earlier solar technology.

timeline.title: Nobel Prize for lithium-ion
timeline.text: Goodenough, Whittingham and Yoshino are honoured.
timeline.why: The battery behind phones and electric cars.

quiz.q: Which fuel stores the most energy per kilogram?
quiz.explain: About 142 MJ/kg, roughly three times petrol, but very little per litre as a gas.

quiz.q: Why is hydrogen hard to store?
options: It has very low density, so it needs high pressure or extreme cold
It is highly toxic, so tanks must be sealed
It is very heavy, so tanks become too large
It is radioactive, so tanks need shielding
quiz.explain: Liquid hydrogen must be kept below −253 °C.

options: Made by electrolysis using renewable electricity
Made from natural gas without capture
Made from coal in gasification plants
quiz.explain: Most hydrogen today comes from fossil fuels.

options: Energy stored per unit mass or volume
The voltage between its two electrodes
How fast it can be charged
quiz.explain: Higher energy density means longer range for the same weight.

quiz.q: In a hydrogen fuel cell, hydrogen and oxygen produce…
quiz.explain: No combustion: the reaction runs electrochemically.

quiz.q: Perovskite solar cells are named after…
options: A crystal structure type, after the mineral perovskite
Pure silicon grown in a special way
quiz.explain: The mineral itself is calcium titanate, CaTiO₃.

quiz.q: Who discovered the photovoltaic effect in 1839?

options: Distilling crude oil at low temperature
They react reversibly with it, and release it when heated
They burn CO₂ to produce energy
They absorb oxygen and leave CO₂ behind
They glow when CO₂ is present

quiz.explain: They trade some energy density for cost and supply security.

quiz.q: Where was the first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction achieved, in 1942?
quiz.explain: Under the stands of a sports field at the University of Chicago.

quiz.q: What did Goodenough's team contribute in 1980?
quiz.explain: It doubled the voltage available from earlier lithium cells.
